Good question, though.

Have you tried researching every minute detail about any particular food, and the effects of all its components? For example if you know every molecule that is in a carrot, and you know how your body benefits from each of those molecules, then you know the carrot cannot be harmful. That's a lot of research work, but it could perhaps clear a few of the simpler foods for you. At least until cognitive dissonance sets back in.

Also, your body is made to handle imperfect foods, just like your muscles respond to excessive weights. First, the bacteria in your digestive track are just bacteria, they have completely different DNA from you, so if you eat something slightly bad it only affects them and not (technically) you. Second, they are hardy motherfuckers and evolution has designed them to handle a lot of shit. They are only interested in consuming, so even if you give them something that makes them sick they are still happy about it.

If I ever don't feel like eating but I know I need to get more protein, I try to imagine all those bacteria shouting "hey brain, you asshole, we're hungry down here!"

Finally, recent research is showing that you are literally better off if you consume things even if your body doesn't like them, because your stomach can handle it better than any other part of you. This is coming out of allergy research. Kids are more likely to become severely allergic to peanuts if their family tries to completely avoid them. It turns out that, if a kid's only contact with peanuts is through the skin or lungs, the body will probably think of it as a toxin and develop an allergic reaction. But if a kid eats peanuts and the first contact is via the stomach, the body will learn that it's a safe food.

Pretty cool, right? It explains why kids try to eat everything they can get their hands on.
